sections.content:
Population change in Bury in 2032

The population in Bury is projected to increase from 194,590 people in 2022 to 198,669 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 6,512 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Bury
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Bury, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 501, with 20,017 births and 20,519 deaths in Bury between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Bury by 0.3%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 1,168, with 91,980 people moving to the area and 93,148 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Bury by 0.6%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 847, with 2,223 people moving to the area and 3,070 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Bury by 0.4%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 6,512, with 12,347 people moving to the area and 5,835 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Bury by 3.3%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Bury in 2032

The median age in Bury is projected to rise from 40 years in 2022 to 41 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 19% of the population in Bury are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 17% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Bury between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Bury is projected to stay the same, at around 64%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to stay around the same, at 278 in 2032 compared with 277 in 2022.

This is around average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Bury?

In 2032, 21% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 24% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Bury between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
